capabilities: Organize a project as a folder-tree writing binder with per-document status and goals
Run focus, typography, and draft/edit/review writing modes
Time writing sprints and track word counts, goals, and streaks
Export the compiled manuscript to Manuscript, PDF, DOCX, RTF, HTML, Markdown, or EPUB
Publish a draft to WordPress and browse vault folders in a sidebar explorer
disambiguation: Not a general Markdown converter or a plain file explorer; it is a manuscript-oriented environment whose binder, outline, and export all operate on one writing project.
extras: Desktop only (Windows, macOS, Linux); requires Obsidian 1.13.0 or later. Manuscript, HTML, Markdown, and EPUB export need no external tools; PDF, DOCX, and RTF require Pandoc, and PDF also needs a LaTeX engine unless wkhtmltopdf is pinned. Typography fonts load from Google Fonts and need internet on first use. WordPress credentials are stored in the plugin's data.json and are lost on manual uninstall/reinstall or a sync conflict. README includes an in-app guide, security scanning details, and a one-time folder rearrangement on upgrading existing projects with a restore command.
problem: Obsidian's editor alone lacks the project structure, focus controls, progress tracking, and export/publishing steps needed to take a nonfiction manuscript from research notes to a finished file.
